iterations.hypothesis: reconstruction of accepted C10 dev-06 base (no runtime change authored)

The dominant ALLOW->REFUSE family built no tax relation at all: the C10 tightening required a TAX_DOMAIN_OBJECT match before a compliance relation, but that vocabulary omitted core instruments and predicates (annual return, final tax, deductible, registration fee), so genuine tax questions fell to the REFUSE fallback. Widened the tax-domain vocabulary, made a governed tax predicate over the target sufficient attachment for a compliance relation, and treated an explanatory verb over a recognised tax acronym or concept as a definition request.

An enumerated metadata suffix never supplies a target, so the contentless guard is evaluated on the metadata-stripped clause; it is exempted when that clause names a tax instrument, a recognised acronym or substantive tax subject matter, which is what protects the richer issuance questions. A governed tax predicate whose subject is a plain definite noun phrase now counts as an anchor. A naming or titling action over a token is label binding even when the token is a statute name.

The metadata-contentless guard cannot be discriminated by whether a tax name appears, because a contentless query and a rich issuance query both name a tax. The real discriminator is whether the metadata-stripped clause has a non-deictic subject of its own. A definite noun-phrase subject governed by an explicit tax predicate is a concrete target and builds the matching treatment relation.

Six structural families: a tax amount or rate whose target follows a preposition; a recognised tax concept in a treatment or application frame over an entity; a procedure scoped to a taxpayer or the revenue authority; a statute named as the subject of a tax question, which defeats the non-tax action reading; a subordinate code clause under a governed tax predicate, which does not make naming primary; and an ordinary personal or social frame, which governs its own target and refuses rather than clarifies.
